 SCCH 15 4 MVC No.5923/2018  :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ for the death of Bylappa S/o Iramallaiah in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 03.01.2016 at about 9.00 a.m., when the deceased Bylappa was proceeding as a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K2832 and when they reached Mullakattamma Temple, CD Agrahara, Madure Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, at that time, the rider of the said motorcycle was ridden in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and skidded the motorcycle.
Due to the impact, said Bylappa had fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

After the accident deceased was shifted to Government Hospital,
Doddaballapura and Post SCCH 15 5 MVC No.5923/2018 mortem was conducted and body was handed over to the Petitioners.
The Petitioners had spent about Rs.1,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was doing Kerosene business and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Bylappa, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 was the owner of the offending motorcycle.
During the pendency, the Respondent No.1 was died and his LR's were brought on record as Respondent No.1(a) to Respondent No.1(d).
The Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K2832.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, both Respondents appeared before the Court through their SCCH 15 6 MVC No.5923/2018 respective counsels and and filed their Written statements to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1(a) to (d) in their Objection Statement and Additional Objection Statement had denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K2832.
Further, they denied the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.

Pujamma vs Channrayappa on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196677416/
3
Further they stated that as on the date of alleged accident, the insurance Policy was in force and rider holds valid and effective DL to ride the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, they have prayed to dismiss the Petition against them.

The Respondent No.2 has filed its detailed Objection Statement interalia denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the death of SCCH 15 7 MVC No.5923/2018 the deceased in the said accident.
Further it contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective riding license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, it has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, deceased Bylappa was died in RTA arising out of accident alleged to have been taken place on 03.01.2016 at about 8.00 a.m.,
Muppadigatta, CD Agrahara road, near Mulkattamma temple, CD Agrahara, Madure hobli, Doddaballapura taluk, Bengaluru rural district, due to rash and negligence riding of rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52 K2832?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the dependents of the deceased?
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5923/2018 3.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
4 . What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 got examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
The Respondent No.1(a) to (d) did not choose to lead evidence.

6. Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon perusal of the depositions,
documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
SCCH 15 9 MVC No.5923/2018 Pujamma vs Channrayappa on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196677416/
4  REASONS 7.
Issue No.1:

It is the case of the Petitioners that the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Bylappa was died in the accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K 2832.
8.
On the other hand, both Respondents had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re iterated the averments made in the petition.
PW.1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.

Ex.P1 is the True copies of FIR with Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Maregowda, the Doddabelavangala Police have registered the case against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K2832 for the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.5923/2018 offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304A of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the True copy of Spot mahazar with Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P3 is the True copy of IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P4 is the True copy of Inquest report.
Ex.P.5 is the True copy of PM report which shows the cause of death is due to Haemorrage and shock due to head injury sustained in RTA.

Ex.P6 is the true copy of the ChargeSheet which shows that the I.O of Doddabelavangala Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC u/s 180, 181, 187 of IMV Act.

The Column No.17 of the Charge Sheet reads as under:
"  279, 304     / 180, 181, 187      01.07.2020   9.00              ,     SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5923/2018                      12    1 .  522832              9                      
                 
            ,  , 
            ,     1             1

,  2                     1           .
            .
Pujamma vs Channrayappa on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196677416/
5 10.
PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.5923/2018 learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
11.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer by name Himendra Kartantik Simha M.N as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4.
In the crossexamination, nothing could be elicited to disprove the contentions of the Petitioners.
Charge sheet is the material document which was submitted by the I.O against the rider of the offending motorcycle after thorough investigation.

Hence, the Petitioners have proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative ".
12. Issue No.2 and 3: All these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5923/2018 13.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and Petitioner No.2 to 7 are the children of the deceased Bylappa.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.2 to 7 at Ex.P.8 to P.13 and Family Ration card at Ex.P7.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
As the Petitioners are the L.Rs of deceased Bylappa, they entitled for the compensation.
14. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 55 years and deceased was doing Kerosene business and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
However, the Inquest Report and PM report, the age of the deceased was shown as 60 years.
Further, Ex.P7 - Ration card shows the age of the deceased at 59 years.
The same was issued on 25.07.2015.
The accident was occurred in the year 2016.
Hence, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 60 years.
Hence, the age of the deceased to be taken at 60 years.
Further the Petitioners SCCH 15 14 MVC No.5923/2018 have not produced the income proof of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.9,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
15. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
16.
The deceased has left behind his wife, daughters and sons.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 to 7 are the children and they are considered as dependents on the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Pujamma vs Channrayappa on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196677416/
6 Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company SCCH 15 15 MVC No.5923/2018 Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)

entities.text: MVC No.5923/2018 Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that :
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No. 2 to 7 are the children of the deceased Bylappa are entitled for a sum of Rupees 40,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 15,000/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
17.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support in her young age and Petitioner No.2 to 7 are the children of deceased and they have lost father's love and care.

Bearing in mind the relationship of the SCCH 15 16 MVC No.5923/2018 Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
18. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
19.
It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased to be taken at Rs.9,500/ pm.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India SCCH 15 17 MVC No.5923/2018
At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.

Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "
 Held :  yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :

sentences.text: 7 "Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40

Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High SCCH 15 18 MVC No.5923/2018 Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation -

Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork: executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 10% when the age is between 50 to 60 years".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was SCCH 15 19 MVC No.5923/2018 aged 60 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 10% of the income has to be added.
So, 10% of Rs.9,500/ comes to Rs.950/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.10,450/ p.m. (Rs.9,500/ + Rs.950/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 9.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to held that where the number of dependent of family members is exceeding 6, 1/5th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

20. After deducting 1/5th towards his personal expenses in Rs.10,450/ it comes to Rs.8,360/
(Rs.10,450/  2,090/) and multiplier applied is 9 which comes to Rs.9,02,880/ (8,360 x 12 x 9).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,02,880/ towards loss of dependency.
SCCH 15 20 MVC No.5923/2018 21. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.
Loss of Dependency Rs.9,02,880/ Total Rs.10,27,880/

Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.10,27,880/ with costs and simple Pujamma vs Channrayappa on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196677416/
8 interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

22. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending SCCH 15 21 MVC No.5923/2018 Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K2832.
In this case, the Respondent No.1(a) to (d) are the LRs of the Respondent No.1 and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of accident.

23. It is the argument of the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2 Insurance company that the rider of the offending motorcycle did not hold the valid driving license at the time of accident and the Charge sheet shows the offences punishable under Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.
However, in the crossexamination of RW.1, he deposed that they did not inquire in the RTO to know whether the rider of the offending motorcycle holds driving license at the time of accident or not.

It is pertinent to note here that the Respondent No.2 has taken steps by filing application before this Court to direct the Respondent No.1 to produce the driving license of the rider of the offending motorcycle at the time of accident.
It is worth to SCCH 15 22 MVC No.5923/2018 note here that the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 has filed Memo along with the copy of driving license of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
Upon going through the said copy of DL, it shows that the said DL was issued on 02.01.2023.
Hence, by taking into consideration of the said fact, this Court has directed the Respondent No.2 to produce the DL of Mr. Keshava Murthy @ Keshava S/o Muniraju before the Court.
But, inspite of sufficient opportunities given, the LR's of deceased Respondent No.1 did not produce DL before the Court.

24. Apart from this, Charge sheet i.e., Ex.P.6 clearly shows that the rider of the offending vehicle was Charge sheeted for the offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and U/s 3 (1) r/w Sec.181, 187 of IMV Act and the owner / insured i.e., Respondent No.1 was Charge sheeted for the offences punishable U/s 180 of IMV Act.
25.
Hence, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident, the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess valid SCCH 15 23 MVC No.5923/2018 driving license.
However, Ex.R2 shows that the Policy of the offending vehicle is in force at the time of accident.

26. In the decision reported in 2004(3) SCC 297 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Swarn Singh and others, wherein, the Hon'ble Appex Court has pleased to held that the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amounts which has been compelled to pay the third party under the award of the Tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Swarn Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Appex Court has highlighted the concept of pay and recovery.

27. It is a settled law that where the driver does not possess a valid driving licence, the insurer would still have to satisfy the compensation and thereafter to recover the said amount from the owner.

Hence, by relying on the above said dictum of Hon'ble Appex Court, this Tribunal is of the opinion that at the first instance, it is necessary to direct the insurer i.e., Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the SCCH 15 24 MVC No.5923/2018 Petitioners and thereafter, recover the same from the LR's of the deceased Respondent No.1 i.e., insured.

Accordingly, I answer Issue Pujamma vs Channrayappa on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196677416/
9 No.2 in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
28. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 7 are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,27,880/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 7 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.10,27,880/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the SCCH 15 25 MVC No.5923/2018 Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1(a) to (d) are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1(a) to (d) through due process of law.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 7 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 88% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 2% each to the Petitioner No.2 to 7.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount SCCH 15 26 MVC No.5923/2018 is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 to 7 is ordered to be paid to them respectively by way of E payment and after their proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/.
 Draw Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to the impact, said Bylappa had fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Due to the death of Bylappa, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 was the owner of the offending motorcycle.
During the pendency, the Respondent No.1 was died and his LR's were brought on record as Respondent No.1(a) to Respondent No.1(d).
The Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K2832.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.1(a) to (d) in their Objection Statement and Additional Objection Statement had denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52K2832.
Further, they denied the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Hence, they are not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 has filed its detailed Objection Statement interalia denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the death of SCCH 15 7 MVC No.5923/2018 the deceased in the said accident.
Further it contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective riding license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners.
opennyai_summary.issue:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, deceased Bylappa was died in RTA arising out of accident alleged to have been taken place on 03.01.2016 at about 8.00 a.m.,
Muppadigatta, CD Agrahara road, near Mulkattamma temple, CD Agrahara, Madure hobli, Doddaballapura taluk, Bengaluru rural district, due to rash and negligence riding of rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA52 K2832?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the dependents of the deceased?
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5923/2018 3.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
4 . What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, the Petitioners have proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, the age of the deceased to be taken at 60 years.
Hence, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.9,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
23. It is the argument of the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2 Insurance company that the rider of the offending motorcycle did not hold the valid driving license at the time of accident and the Charge sheet shows the offences punishable under Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.
But, inspite of sufficient opportunities given, the LR's of deceased Respondent No.1 did not produce DL before the Court.
24. Apart from this, Charge sheet i.e., Ex.P.6 clearly shows that the rider of the offending vehicle was Charge sheeted for the offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and U/s 3 (1) r/w Sec.181, 187 of IMV Act and the owner / insured i.e., Respondent No.1 was Charge sheeted for the offences punishable U/s 180 of IMV Act.
25.
Hence, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident, the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess valid SCCH 15 23 MVC No.5923/2018 driving license.
However, Ex.R2 shows that the Policy of the offending vehicle is in force at the time of accident.
27. It is a settled law that where the driver does not possess a valid driving licence, the insurer would still have to satisfy the compensation and thereafter to recover the said amount from the owner.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, by relying on the above said dictum of Hon'ble Appex Court, this Tribunal is of the opinion that at the first instance, it is necessary to direct the insurer i.e., Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the SCCH 15 24 MVC No.5923/2018 Petitioners and thereafter, recover the same from the LR's of the deceased Respondent No.1 i.e., insured.
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 7 are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,27,880/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 7 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.10,27,880/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the SCCH 15 25 MVC No.5923/2018 Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1(a) to (d) are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1(a) to (d) through due process of law.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 7 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 88% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 2% each to the Petitioner No.2 to 7.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount SCCH 15 26 MVC No.5923/2018 is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 to 7 is ordered to be paid to them respectively by way of E payment and after their proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/.
 Draw Award accordingly.
